thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for model-runner-prod (region: us-west-2). Error spike started ~ 4165002300, current 5xx rate 18% (baseline 0.4%). Paging on-call.

pager-duty: paging maya (primary oncall) — can you ack and take a look? :pager:

maya: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs now.

kevin: ping if you need infra help. we can lift some extra capacity in the pool.

maya: quick summary from prometheus: model-runner service pods report continuous 502/504 and several 5xx spikes. CPU is fine, GPU mem usage is high on a subset of nodes. Autoscaler hasn't moved yet. I'll pull pod logs.

olga: possible segfault/OOM? we saw similar pattern last month when kv-cache was corrupted.

maya: pasting last 50 lines from model-runner stderr (pod: mr-49a2):
```
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] runtime: panic: double free detected
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] goroutine 54 [running]:
	runtime.throw(0x7f1a23, 0x10)
		/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:1198 +0x72
	runtime.free(0xc0003f0000)
		/usr/local/go/src/runtime/mem.go:424 +0x33
...
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] inference: model-runner: segfault at 0x0
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] kernel: [  120.345678] model-runner[17219]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f2a... sp 00007fffa... error 6 in libruntime.so
```

kevin: that looks like a native segfault inside the native kernel (CUDA path) - check dmesg for OOM/kern logs on the node.

maya: grabbing dmesg from node gpu-12:
```
Mar 15 10:04:59 gpu-12 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 17219 (model-runner) total-vm:14000000kB, anon-rss:12000000kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
Mar 15 10:04:59 gpu-12 kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 17219 (model-runner), now anon-rss:0kB
Mar 15 10:04:59 gpu-12 nvidia: Out of memory on GPU 0: attempted alloc 8.0GB, free 2.3GB
```

olga: confirmed OOM on GPU. Might be a runaway batch or KV cache growth. Any recent model rollouts? config changes?

sam: I rolled out quant-mode=true flag to a subset of pods 20m ago as an experiment. That changes memory allocation paths - could be related.

maya: ok roll that back on the rollback-canary group. Patching Deployment to set quant-mode=false now.

kevin: starting a node drain loop for gpu-12 to repro locally then rotate. I'll also spin up two extra gpu nodes to reduce immediate pressure.

incident-bot: ACTION LOG: maya set quant-mode=false on deployment/model-runner at 4165002420.

maya: rolling restarts in progress. I'm also flipping KVCACHE_ENABLED=false on the affected deployment to avoid prefix cache growth.

emily-support: support note: customer-orga1 reporting latency spikes and 502s since ~10:04 UTC. They've opened a ticket (TICKET-9821). Marking incident for customer-impact.

maya: thanks emily. Can someone run a selective failover to the fallback-model (smaller 7B quantized) for high-latency routes? Prefer graceful fallback to avoid 502s for customer-orga1.

sam: initiating routing override: route /api/v1/generate for customer-orga1 -> model=fallback-7b at 4165002485. Will monitor.

kevin: nodes up + autoscaler override applied (scale to +2 GPUs) at 4165002490. Watch for stabilization.

maya: current status: restarts completed for 6/8 pods in canary; 2 pods still crash on start with immediate segfault. Logs show native abort when allocating KV cache region.

olga: can we disable kernel page cache / reduce rlimit? Might be hitting a kernel bug with large pinned memory allocations.

kevin: adding vm.overcommit_memory=1 and bumping swappiness temporarily on gpu nodes (applied at 4165002520). Also applied nvidia driver recommended KMS workaround.

incident-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for 10m during mitigation window.

maya: after changes, observed 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3.5% over last 2m. customer-orga1 error rate in their region down to 1.2%. Still watching.

emily-support: updating ticket TICKET-9821: "We observed 502/504s earlier caused by model-runner pod OOMs in us-west-2; engineering applied fallbacks and rolled back quant experiment. Continued monitoring. ETA for postmortem: 24h." :white_check_mark:

sam: follow-up tasks: (1) revert quant experiment flags globally, (2) add memory/kvcache guardrails in runtime config, (3) add circuit-breaker to route to fallback model on >5% 5xx for a customer within 1m.

maya: agree. immediate mitigations worked. I'll keep the incident open for a formal postmortem. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause analysis.

kevin: I'll capture kernel oops and create a node-level repro. pushing driver logs to artifact store: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/4165002345/driver-logs.tar.gz

olga: QA note: add a smoke test that exercises kv-cache growth under long prefix workloads.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=sev2, impacted_customers=[customer-orga1], affected_regions=[us-west-2], mitigation_summary=[rolled back quant experiment, disabled kv cache, scaled +2 GPU nodes, route override to fallback-7b], status=stabilized.

maya: stepping off-call in 15m. sam will take second-stage until postmortem scheduled.

sam: taking over. will run through checklist and confirm postmortem owners.

maya: close monitoring for 60m, but action items assigned. leaving notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4165002345

emily-support: sending customer update now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (stabilized) at 4165002665 — auto-close after 60m of stability. Summary and playbook links attached in incident doc.

sam: thanks everyone. we'll lock a postmortem owners meeting for 10:30 UTC tomorrow.

olga: thumbs up :thumbsup:

maya: great work team."
